notes.markdown:
ACARS from aircraft on the radio's own decoder, a pager mode for POCSAG, an APRS Traffic list, the owner card on the
PIN screen, and fixes for the clicks beside broadcast FM, the tone from the screen light and the three known issues
from 0.9.7. Ferrite Console 0.9.8 comes with it: update both together.

## Before you update

- **Charge the radio to over 50% first.** An update on a low battery (25% or less) can stop part way. Console will
  check the battery for you from 0.9.9.
- **Update Ferrite Console too.** Console 0.9.8 knows the pager settings and draws Live View in the radio's theme;
  Console 0.9.7 doesn't.

## New

- **ACARS (on trial).** Tools › ACARS (MENU 0 3 8) listens on an ACARS frequency (131.550, 131.725 and others) and
  decodes aircraft messages with the radio's own decoder. Ten messages to a page on two lines each, repeats counted on
  one row, `*` marks messages with text. A message page shows the flight, airline and text; data reports say what
  kind they are and how long, rather than a wall of hex. Airline names come once Console has written its table.
- **Pager mode for POCSAG.** Slot C can listen for pages as it listens for APRS: turn on Decode (MENU 0 4 2 2), and
  pages land in Messages, read like APRS messages. Frequency, speed and a capcode filter are in 0 4 2. While Pager
  mode listens, home's scope strip doesn't sweep slot C's receiver, as with APRS.
- **APRS Traffic** (the APRS menu's item 8): every packet heard lately, newest first, two lines each. A station's
  Message line in Heard now shows the last message it sent to anyone, with "to CALL:". A message to another of your
  SSIDs shows in Traffic, not in your inbox.
- **The owner card on the power-on PIN screen:** "If found, please contact", then the name (larger), callsign, phone
  and e-mail you've set in Console's owner card.
- **Power on reopens the tool you had open**: the band scope, counter, HF mode, tone search, the satellite screen,
  SSTV, ACARS or crossband, after the boot screen and the PIN.
- **Quick menu (hold \*): PTT B steps night red, then daylight, then back** to your usual theme.
- **8.33 kHz airband channels by their names:** type 118.010 and the radio tunes 118.00833 and shows 118.010, as
  printed on charts.
- **Broadcast FM reads WFM** on its slot card and on the Status screen.
- **The SSB patch over the link:** Console can now add SSB to a radio already on Ferrite, over the cable or Bluetooth,
  without reinstalling.
- **"Unofficial build"** shows in amber on About for any image that isn't an official release, so a changed build is
  easy to tell apart.

## Changed

- **Home's S-meter is empty while the squelch is closed,** as on stock firmware. Press monitor, or open the squelch
  screen, to see the level and noise floor. The squelch editor's "Signal now" bar reads the live level.
- **The transmit duty limit follows power:** High fills it at full rate, Mid at half, Low at a quarter (from cold,
  about 4, 8 and 16 minutes of continuous transmit), and it cools twice as fast as before.
- **The screen light switches at about 31.7 kHz,** well above hearing.

## Fixed

- **Clicks with other slots on watch beside broadcast FM** (ferrite#179). A watch turn to a slot set up differently
  no longer retunes the shared receiver audibly.
- **A tone on receive that followed the screen brightness** (ferrite#271, and Console's report of a whine in HF mode).
  The screen light's switching was in the audio range.
- **Colours on the screen could invert after some hours** (ferrite#182). The screen's settings are now sent again on
  wake and every 10 seconds.
- **Automatic transmissions now wait** while HF mode, the band scope, the counter, tone search or the satellite
  screen is open: beacons, KISS frames and message retries go out once you leave (0.9.7's known issue, ferrite#131).
- **While a single-receiver mode runs** (band scope, counter, tone search, HF, satellite, crossband), the slots it
  isn't reading show closed: no stale busy state or audio (0.9.7's known issue, ferrite#132).
- **Squelch 0 with the scope strip** (Single + scope layout): the strip now holds on its slot, open, with audio, as
  monitor does (0.9.7's known issue, ferrite#140, #44).
- **APRS on slot C could go deaf for about a second** beside a range scan on the other receiver (ferrite#143).
- **The S-meter of a slot nothing is reading** showed its last level; it's now empty.
- **Cut-off text:** a refused transmit's message, the editors' slot strip, the crossband line in HF mode, the Low
  Power Mode line and the satellite HD note.
- **Terminal `load` at full speed** could lose lines with XON/XOFF; it now pauses earlier and refuses a line with lost
  bytes rather than taking it.
- **Sturdier against damaged packets:** new tests feed every decoder damaged and endless input, checking for hangs as
  well as crashes.

## Known issues

- **A radio froze after APRS traffic** for one user (ferrite#73). We haven't been able to make it happen; if it does
  for you, please add what the radio was doing to the issue.

Narrow AM for the airband with a proper 8.33 kHz step, APRS messages to your plain callsign and to CQ, Mic gain up to
12, SSB past 18 MHz as an experiment, and a long list of fixes from your reports and from new crash-hunting tests.
Ferrite Console 0.9.7 comes with it: update both together.

## Before you update

- **Update Ferrite Console too.** Console 0.9.7 knows NAM (narrow AM) and the new checks on channel writes; Console
  0.9.6 doesn't.
- **The airband now starts in NAM** (narrow AM) when you tune a VFO there. Channels and VFOs already set to AM stay
  AM.

## New

- **NAM, narrow AM, for the airband.** AM through the radio's narrow receive filter: an 8.33 kHz neighbour that came
  through at full strength on AM is now rejected, and the station you're on keeps its level. It's the airband's
  default in every region, and choosing the 8.33 kHz step (MENU 6) on an AM slot turns it on. Receive only, as AM.
- **The 8.33 kHz step stays on the airband channel grid.** It used to move a flat 8.330 kHz and drifted off the
  channels after a few steps; three steps are now exactly 25 kHz.
- **Messages to CQ, QST and ALL** show at the top of your APRS messages (MENU 0 5 2) for 30 minutes, newest first,
  with a short notice when one arrives and an entry in the event log. They aren't acked and don't play the message
  sound, so a busy net doesn't keep the radio chiming. OK opens one; OK again writes its sender a reply.
- **A message shows who it was sent to:** open a message to you and it says "To VE7GPL" or "To VE7GPL-7" under the
  sender (for messages received from 0.9.7 on). A station's page in Heard shows who its last message was to.
- **Mic gain goes to 12** (MENU 0 8 3). 1 to 9 are as before; 10, 11 and 12 add about 3, 5 and 8 dB for quiet mics,
  a speaker mic mostly. A speaker mic still gets one step more than Mic gain. On a narrow channel a loud voice at 10
  to 12 can go past the allowed deviation: turn it up only as far as your mic needs.
- **The mic meter shows the gain** on the transmit screen: it used to read the same at any Mic gain.
- **SSB up to 30 MHz (experimental).** HF mode (MENU 0 3 3) now offers USB, LSB and CW on 17 m, 15 m, 12 m and 10 m,
  on the radio's broadcast receiver. That chip is only specified to 23 MHz, and we couldn't test it on the air past
  18 MHz, so results may vary: going there shows "Experimental / please report". Please tell us on GitHub or Discord
  how it works for you, band by band. AM and FM above 18 MHz are unchanged.
- **NFM on CB and the other bands from 18 to 64 MHz**, on home VFOs and channels, alongside FM and AM. A CB
  channel's mode now steps FM, NFM, AM (it used to be stuck on FM).
- **Satellites: the display stays lit around a pass.** With the satellite screen open, from 5 minutes before a pass
  rises to 5 minutes after it sets, the screen doesn't go dark and auto power off waits.
- **SSTV receive: # picks the mode** (Robot 36, Martin M1, Scottie S1, PD90, PD120 or Auto) and says which.
- **Broadcast FM channels show their name** beside the frequency.
- **Waypoints can be deleted**: Delete in a waypoint's options, after a confirmation.

## Fixed

- **No audio after stopping a scan.** The slot showed the frequency it started on, but the receiver stayed where the
  scan had stopped: silence on a channel, or the scanned frequency's audio on a VFO, until you turned the knob. It
  now retunes on every stop, and also when PTT or Low Power Mode stops the scan.
- **Holding ◀ or ▶ to leave broadcast FM raced through several bands**. A hold now steps one band.
- **APRS messages to your callsign without its SSID were lost.** With your radio set to, say, VE7GPL-7, a message to
  VE7GPL now reaches your inbox and is acked, as any message to you.
- **Messages you send to a callsign without an SSID** stopped retrying once that station acked from its own SSID
  (sent to VE7GPL, acked by VE7GPL-7).
- **APRS on slot C could go deaf for about a second** at a time beside a range scan on the other receiver.
- **Scan:** "skip for good" on the last channel left went straight back to it, and a priority look could stop on a
  skipped or empty priority channel.
- **The Watch + activity layout ignored the S-meter setting** (MENU 0 7 3 1) and always showed S-units on its
  cards; with dBm chosen they now read, for example, "RX -93 dBm".
- **Menu rows show the setting**, not a placeholder: 0 1 5, 0 3 1, 0 4 5, 0 7 3, 0 7 5 and 0 8 5.
- **Low Power Mode refuses tone search,** as it does the frequency counter, instead of running it with the receiver
  kept awake.
- **The transmit time limit filled too slowly** on Low power: continuous transmitting reached it after 10 minutes
  instead of 8.
- **The tone picker** carried typed digits over after the arrows.
- **A few screens left stale pixels** after some key sequences (Low Power Mode's home, the transmit screen, the
  transmit-refused dialog).
- **Help lines:** POCSAG's mentioned a speed setting that didn't exist; 0 9 9's listed a bench-only item.
- **The HF screen's step line** ran out of room with a 12.5 kHz step.
- **Sturdier against damaged data.** New tests that press every key on every screen, in odd states, and feed the
  radio damaged records and link messages found a set of rare faults, now fixed: a damaged zone record no longer
  hides its channels, a damaged settings record can't set a nonsense scan priority, the GPS, grid square and SAME
  decoders handle out-of-range numbers, and the link refuses channel and zone values the radio's own editor can't
  produce, with a reason.

## Known issues

- **Beacons and KISS frames can still go out while HF mode, the band scope, the counter or the satellite screen is
  open** (ferrite#131). Turn beacons or Tracker off while you use those, for now.
- **While the band scope, counter, tone search, HF, satellite or crossband mode runs, slot C's squelch state stays as
  it was when the mode started** (ferrite#132).
- **Squelch at 0 can stay closed** for some users on some layouts (ferrite#140). Monitor (SIDE1) opens it meanwhile.
  We're collecting details on the issue.

SSTV pictures, a simpler APRS setting, no more clicks, a louder mic, and fixes from your reports. Ferrite Console 0.9.6 comes with
it: update both together.

## Before you update

- **Beacons with APRS mode off:** if your radio sent position beacons with APRS mode (MENU 0 5 3) off, it won't after
  the update. Set 0 5 3 to **Tracker** to keep beaconing. See APRS below.
- **Update Ferrite Console too.** Console 0.9.5 shows the APRS settings read only on 0.9.6, and Console 0.9.6 does the
  same on 0.9.5.
- **Mic gain:** a radio still on the old default (5) moves to the new default, 8. A gain you chose yourself stays.

## New

- **SSTV pictures (MENU 0 3 7).** Receive pictures on the active slot (Robot 36, Martin M1, Scottie S1, PD90 and
  PD120); the two newest are kept. Send one back, a picture from Ferrite Console, or the built-in test card with your
  callsign, in Robot 36, Martin M1, Scottie S1 or PD90. Watch and scans pause while the screen is open. Ferrite Console
  has an SSTV page to see the pictures and set the one to send.
- **APRS mode is one setting (MENU 0 5 3): Off, Tracker, On or KISS.**
  - **Tracker** sends your position beacons and nothing else: no decoding, no messages. It's what "beacons with APRS
    mode off" used to be, now named.
  - **On** is the full APRS mode, as before.
  - **KISS** hands the radio to an APRS app; 0 5 8 picks its port (Cable or Bluetooth).
- **APRS message retries** (Messages options): off, or 1 to 4 tries.
- **Type + in APRS messages:** on the 1 key, after the colon.
- **The PTT picks the mic.** Stock always talks through the speaker mic once one is plugged in, whichever PTT you
  press. Ferrite now goes by the PTT you press:
  - **The speaker mic's PTT** transmits on the speaker mic, as before.
  - **The radio's own PTT** (either of its PTT keys) transmits on the radio's built-in mic, with the speaker mic still
    plugged in. Handy when the speaker mic is clipped somewhere you can't talk into it, or when it's the quieter of
    the two.
  - **A key-up without a PTT** (VOX, a key-up from Ferrite Console or Pocket, an APRS beacon or SSTV picture) uses the
    speaker mic, as stock does.
  - Receive audio stays on the speaker mic whichever you used, and comes back to it as soon as you let go.
  - **Seeing which mic is on:** the status bar shows **SPK** while a speaker mic is connected, and the transmit screen
    names the mic in use ("Spk mic" or "Radio mic") beside the mic meter, which now moves for either mic.
  - **Speaker mic level:** a key-up on the speaker mic runs one Mic gain step higher than the radio's own mic (9 at
    the default 8), as speaker mics are usually quieter.
- **Satellites: hold 2** on the pass or pointing page cycles the uplink power.
- **Scan: stopping stays on what the scan found.** MENU 0 1 6 4 (Return to) now starts on Last hit for new radios;
  a radio set to Start keeps it.
- **Range presets:** SIDE2 in the preset list scans the preset, and the Scan menu shows how many there are.
- **Single + scope layout:** # pauses the scope strip, so APRS and the watch can listen; # again sweeps. With the
  strip paused and a watched slot receiving, # pauses the watch, as on the other layouts.
- **Range scans: # on a hit skips that frequency** in the preset's skip list (up to 48), and the scan carries on.
- **Clearing a whole list asks first:** # on the Skip list (MENU 0 1 5) and on HF mode's recent list.

## Fixed

- **Saving stopped working on some radios** until they were switched off and on. On radios with a Zbit flash chip
  (many of them), a read at the wrong moment could leave a write stuck. Fixed, along with how the radio picks up its
  flash after a restart.
- **Clicks in broadcast FM, while scanning and in satellite mode.** Since 0.9.5 every retune briefly switched the
  receiver chip off, which clicked in whatever was playing. A frequency change no longer does. Beside broadcast FM the
  watch now hops without a sound, and in satellite mode the downlink retunes only once the Doppler drift passes
  1 kHz.
- **Noise on 2 m and 70 cm from the backlights** (on 146.075 MHz, for example). The screen and keypad lights now dim at
  2 kHz.
- **Your voice was too quiet on the air.** Mic gain now defaults to 8, louder than stock's, and goes up to 9; a speaker
  mic gets one step more. The mic meter on the transmit screen works with a speaker mic too.
- **The radio's own PTT sent nothing with a speaker mic plugged in.** See "The PTT picks the mic" above.
- **APRS beacons and SSTV pictures didn't go out while broadcast FM played.** Broadcast now pauses for them, as it
  does for PTT, and comes back after.
- **An APRS beacon could cut an SSTV picture short.** Beacons, acks and retries now wait until the picture is sent,
  and the next timed beacon counts from when the last one actually went out.
- **Satellites: a second PTT while the first transmission was ending restarted the radio.**
- **Satellites, full duplex: the uplink could carry the access tone but not your voice.**
- **SSB sometimes stayed silent** after switching to it: the patch now loads at a speed the receiver chip handles
  reliably.
- **Reverse didn't listen on the input frequency,** and showed no R. Fixed.
- **GPS Auto didn't turn the GPS on for the satellite screen,** or for Tracker's beacons.
- **APRS was deaf with the Single + scope layout:** the strip took the receiver. See # above.
- **APRS on a slot C left on AM airband decoded nothing** with the Single + scope layout: the strip was sweeping
  around C's airband frequency. See # above; slot C also shows FM while APRS holds it.
- **The Beacon row (0 5 6) always said Off.**
- **A stopped radio (after repeated restarts) can be switched off** with the power switch.
- **The channel page's name box and the callsign rows** were drawn over.
- **HF mode went silent after a key-up** (PTT on 10 m or 6 m, or a beacon) until you retuned.
- **A monitor latched on one slot left the next slot deaf** after you changed slots: changing slots now turns it off,
  and says so.
- **Night Red: the selected row couldn't be seen** in compose's quick messages and the address book.
- **Satellite mode is off in Low Power Mode,** as the other modes that keep both receivers busy are.
- **Clearer messages:** the watch-pause toast names the time you set (MENU 0 1 6 1), the transmit-refused screen points
  to the right place (MENU 0 0 for the battery, MENU 0 8 8 4 for Extend TX), and a few hints and help lines say
  what the radio actually does.

## Known issues

- **Beacons and KISS frames can still go out while HF mode, the band scope, the counter or the satellite screen is
  open** (ferrite#131). Turn beacons or Tracker off while you use those, for now.
- **While the band scope, counter, tone search, HF, satellite or crossband mode runs, slot C's squelch state stays as
  it was when the mode started** (ferrite#132). If C was hearing a packet just then, the radio can draw a little more
  current, and APRS's busy check can read the old state (a beacon reported "busy", or sent without checking).

Released Nov 21, 2026 (v0.9.5 on ferrite, console, docs and docs-public). Two GitHub releases from this file: the Ferrite part as Ferrite's, the Console part as Console's (as 0.9.4 was).

At release:

- [x] The counter catching a carrier: black's counter read clear on Dry TX at 145.495 (145.49501) and the bladeRF at 433.92 and 446.475 beside a strong VHF signal (TSRCH-10.3), Nov 21, 2026. 915 and 1270 MHz reach chip 1 too weak through the front end (hardware).
- [x] Squelch and scan, second full pass on black (bladeRF, sqreg.py: 44 of 48, the four misses the bench's noise floor and the front end) and with clear as the source (realradio.py: CTCSS plays, a wrong tone stays muted), Nov 21, 2026.
- [ ] Not done by release: Mic gain on the air (another radio listening, a speaker mic too).
- [ ] Not done by release: Console's High speed fix and Bluetooth's step to 9600 on a real radio.
- [ ] Not confirmed by release: Germany's 70 cm repeater offset, built as 7.6 MHz (DL's usual; Alex had said "7.2 I think").
- [x] The reader and restorer images rebuilt and signed by CI with the flash changes (SAFE-1.1, SAFE-1.2), and bundled in Console 0.9.5.
- [x] Console e2e: the CHIRP round trip fixed (Console #38); the full e2e passes on main (144 of 145 at release, the reorder test flaky under load: 3 of 3 alone), Nov 21, 2026.

Fixes from your reports, and a few things made clearer. Ferrite Console 0.9.5 comes with it.

## Fixed

- **The mic was too quiet on the air,** through a speaker mic most of all. Mic gain (MENU 0 8 3) now goes as loud as stock at 9, in 2.5 dB steps; 5, the default, stays where stock starts. If people say you're quiet, try 7 or 8.
- **Monitor didn't work in many places.** SIDE1 now monitors on every screen that doesn't use SIDE1 for something else: Satellites, the menus, Scan and the rest, with the keys locked too. It also works with home's scope strip on (Single + scope): before, MON showed on the card but nothing played until you opened a menu.
- **Satellites: the alarm picker was drawn over.** On a pass page, the countdown and the live values kept redrawing on top of the alarm picker. The page now holds still while the picker is open.
- **Satellites: times cut off.** "Rises in 62:45" on the pointing page now reads "rises 1h02", and a pass that's up shows its time to set in full in the list.
- **The frequency counter missed UHF next to a strong transmitter.** The VHF receiver picked up junk from the strong UHF carrier, which kept the UHF receiver from ever getting its turn. Both receivers now count at once, and junk on one can't hide a reading on the other. VHF works as before.
- **Setting a custom repeater offset showed a popup and closed it.** See Offsets below.
- **The transmitter could stay keyed after a refused key-up.** If the radio had refused a key-up earlier (a low battery under load, say), the next one could be taken as refused on screen while the radio transmitted, with nothing to unkey it until the 10-minute backstop. Fixed: only a refusal after your key-up counts, and a refusal always unkeys.
- **Settings changed just before switching off were sometimes lost** (a VFO change, for example): now saved before the power goes.
- **Satellites: the uplink's Doppler retune while transmitting now passes the same checks as a key-up** (band plan, emergency frequencies, the power table); one that fails ends the transmission.
- **APRS messages from the internet now arrive.** Messages and acks relayed by an IGate from APRS-IS (other stations, SMSGTE, EMAIL-2, WXBOT) were dropped, so a message sent to one of those services showed "failed" even when it was delivered.
- **A zone could end up with more than 256 channels** after a big write from Console; now the write is refused with "zone full" instead.
- **Squelch works as stock's again.** The radio chip decides when the squelch opens, as on the stock firmware, with stock's short hold so a weak or fluttery signal doesn't chop, and a tone (CTCSS/DCS) that misses a beat no longer mutes the audio. Every radio starts on Chip after the update, whatever 0 9 5 was; the older software squelch stays under 0 9 5 Software.
- **Squelch, more fixes:**
  - Setting the level (SIDE1 held + knob) also opened monitor if you held SIDE1 a moment first, so the level seemed to do nothing; now you hear it open and close as you turn.
  - Each step of the level briefly dropped the audio; not any more.
  - On a single slot (watch off) the software squelch took 150 ms to open and a weak, fluttery signal was chopped; it opens sooner now and rides a single noisy moment.
  - With squelch 0 or monitor on, busy lockout refused PTT on an empty channel and the green LED stayed lit; both now follow a real signal.
  - The squelch screen shows the signal and noise floor under the threshold.
  - Scanning and APRS kept their squelch tail too short (a register written at the wrong bits).
- **Tapping OK to skip the owner card at power-on opened the settings reset prompt.** A tap now skips the card; holding MENU from power-on still asks for the reset.
- **Channels and settings didn't stay on some radios.** Radios ship with flash chips from different makers (Winbond, Zbit, Macronix so far). Ferrite now drives the chip the way the stock firmware does, and reads back everything it writes, so a write that didn't take is reported instead of lost. Backups on those radios should read cleanly too.
- **The 12 h clock showed only on the GPS screen.** With MENU 0 6 6 on 12 h, the status bar and the satellite pass times now read `2:32p` (UTC stays 24 h).
- **Home kept bits of the old layout** when the layout was changed from Ferrite Console or the terminal while home was on screen.

## Offsets

- **Hold 7** opens the shift's choices: simplex, +, −, and Split. Each one shows the frequency you'd transmit on.
- **Hold 8** types the offset itself in MHz (7 \* 6 is 7.6). ▲ makes it +, ▼ makes it −, and the TX frequency follows as you type.
- Picking + or − keeps an amount you've set.
- **Europe:** the 70 cm offset is now 7.6 MHz down (2 m stays 600 kHz), from the region you chose at setup.

## Clearer

- **NFM everywhere.** The home cards said "FM-N"; it's NFM now, as everywhere else.
- **The Mode editor (MENU 3) shows each mode's width:** FM · 25 kHz, NFM · 12.5 kHz, WFM · broadcast. MENU's help line says the same.
- **WFM is receive only.** PTT on a WFM slot now says "WFM is broadcast: RX only" and points you to FM or NFM.
- **Status bar:** an amber VOX mark while VOX is on, and the GPS icon is green with a dot once it has a fix (dim grey while searching).
- **The scan button (SIDE2) does nothing in Satellites,** tapped or held.
- **Better bug reports:** Ferrite Console's Save debug info now includes the radio's own report (its flash chip, whether its storage started, calibration, the chips, what's stored), which helps us sort out problems faster.

## Fixed

- **High speed did nothing** (Chrome, Edge and the Windows app). Ticking High speed in Live View switched the cable to 230400, then Console stopped reading it: it gave up and stayed at 115200, or reconnected. Fixed: the bar now says 230400 baud.
- **Only signed firmware installs** unless you tick Allow unsigned files (for your own builds): a bare .btf, the backup reader and the restorer included, and the update feed only ever offers a signed .ffw.
- **Update asks you to turn the radio off and on first** when it runs Ferrite 0.9.4 or earlier: on some radios 0.9.4 left the memory chip stuck, and only switching off clears it.
- **Save debug info says more about the radio.** With a radio connected, the file now carries the radio's own report and what its screen shows (Ferrite 0.9.5 for the report; older firmware gives the screen only).
- **Bluetooth lost data at the edge of range.** Long reads (the satellite list, channels) stalled for seconds and asked again. When Bluetooth at 115200 keeps losing data, Console now drops to 9600 by itself and says so in the bar. Slower, but it gets through. A new Connect tries 115200 again.

- **A write that didn't check out could lose channels.** If the read-back after a write differed, Console replaced your table with what the radio held, so channels that never reached the radio were gone. Now your edits stay, and Write shows what's left to send. A read that comes back short of the radio's channel count is refused instead of being taken as a backup (Console #40).
- **CHIRP import kept your own channels' zones** in the round trip (Console #38).

## Videos

- **A Videos page** with the short feature videos, and one plays while an update runs. They load from ferritefw.dev, so they need the internet; without it the page says so and the update goes on as usual.

## Reorder channels and zones

- **Channels:** drag a channel by its ⠿ handle, or focus the handle and press ↑ ↓. It takes the number you drop it on, and the channels in between move along one. Typing a number that's already used in the channel panel does the same.
- **In a zone** (the Zones tab): drag a channel, or use ▲ ▼. Only that zone's channels change numbers.
- **Zones:** drag a zone in the list, or use ▲ ▼ by its name. Its channels go with it.
- Priority channels and the home channel follow their channels. Each move is one Undo.
- On the radio, a slot stays on its channel *number*: after Write, a slot on a moved number tunes whatever is there now.

## Get it

- macOS (Apple silicon and Intel): the `.dmg`, signed and notarized.
- Linux: the `.AppImage` (or the `.rpm`).
- Windows: the portable `.exe`.
- In the browser: [console.ferritefw.dev](https://console.ferritefw.dev).
- Installed Consoles on macOS and the Linux AppImage offer the update themselves.

Bugs and ideas: [GitHub issues](https://github.com/FerriteFW/console/issues). After a problem, About › Save debug info… and attach the file. Questions: the Ferrite Discord, https://discord.gg/fYygBVD2Kx

## Firmware

- **The heard list names the alternate symbols right.** A station using APRS's alternate symbol table showed under the wrong name: a house (HF) as a handheld, an SUV as a truck, a work zone as a car, "radios and devices" as a boat, a wall cloud as a handheld. They now follow the APRS 1.2 tables.

- **# is help.** A single `#` on home opens the help pages, starting with every hold (ABC, V/M, MENU, BACK, \*, # and the ten digits), then the keys, side keys and menu numbers; `#` again for the next page, `BACK` to leave. The boot screen says so. The Status page is now `MENU 0 0`. While a watched slot is receiving, `#` still pauses watch.
- **The A·B·C key is called ABC,** as it is printed, on the radio and in the guide. The home hint bar says **Hold ABC: Edit**, the slot's settings, in place of "SLOT A·B·C".
- **The APRS list loses "Beacon on/off".** It only paused timed beacons, did nothing with Manual and showed no state. The beacon is set in one place, `MENU 0 5 6 1`; the list's last three rows move up one (5 Event log, 6 Clear the heard list, 7 APRS settings).
- **The channel editor's top line no longer cuts the channel number:** the zone box now starts after it (CH 1000 and up too).
- **The zone editor's priorities show the channel's name** (number and name together were cut at the right edge).
- **Home keeps updating under "PTT stuck".** The popup stays up as long as PTT is held; home's receive and transmit state no longer freeze under it.
- **Beacon now from the link.** Ferrite Console (and later the phone app) can send a position beacon, with the same checks as the radio's own Beacon now.
- **Tuning from Console behaves better.** A scan started from Console no longer replaces the screen you are using on the radio (the scan screen opens only over home); in channel-only mode Console can tune only the active slot; the APRS slot no longer reports its parked channel.

## Updating

A radio on 0.8.x: Console's Update page, or Install › Advanced with `ferrite-0.8.3.ffw`. Your channels and settings stay.
